title: What Happens When Your Ears Pop?
description:
A narrow passage called the eustachian tube links each middle ear to the back of your nose and throat. It stays shut until you swallow, yawn or chew; then it opens, air gets in, and the pressure on both sides of your eardrum evens out. On a plane the pressure can change faster than the tube can adjust, so hearing goes muffled. If ear discomfort, fullness or muffled hearing lasts more than a few days, or is severe, see a doctor.
